        - type: object
          properties:
            id:

              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName,

              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'
                where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the
                upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN a per-city 4-digit
                zero-padded sequence (one more than the owners already in that city).
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'LON-SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable shared identifier for owners in the same household
                (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner is created with
                'sharesHousehold' true; null otherwise.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F60718'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners that shared this owner's first

              format: int32
              minimum: 0

              readOnly: true

## Summary

I implemented the `bulkSignupWarning` rule for `POST /api/owners`, following the codebase's established pattern for derived owner attributes (identical to how `namesakeCount` is computed at create time, stored on the entity, and auto-mapped to the DTO). This guarantees the create response and any later `GET /api/owners/{id}` return a consistent value.

**Changes:**

1. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `bulkSignupWarning` boolean to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` (and every endpoint that returns owners) carries the field.

2. **`Owner.java`** — added the `bulkSignupWarning` (`Boolean`, column `bulk_signup_warning`) field with getter/setter, mirroring `namesakeCount`.

3. **`FlagBulkSignup.java`** (new function class) — counts the owners already created for this owner's registration date (the same per-day accumulation `RequireDailyCapacity` uses) and sets `bulkSignupWarning = count > 80`. It runs before the owner is saved, so it counts existing owners — "more than 80 have *already* been created today."

4. **`owners.POST.yml`** — inserted the `flagBulkSignup` step (transaction-governed) after `countNamesakes` and before `save`, so it runs after the registration date is applied and before persistence.

5. **Schema files** (hsqldb/h2/postgres/mysql `schema.sql`) — added the `bulk_signup_warning BOOLEAN` column. The tests use HSQLDB, whose seed `data.sql` uses positional INSERTs, so I added a trailing `NULL` to each of the 10 owner rows to match the new column count. (MapStruct auto-maps the field — no mapper change needed.)

**Verification:** `./mvnw -o test` → `BUILD SUCCESS`, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`. `AcceptanceTest.coreNoBulkWarningUnderThreshold` (create one owner, then GET expecting `bulkSignupWarning: false`) passes, and the >80 branch reuses the same counting path exercised by the daily-limit rule.

One design note worth surfacing: I interpreted "created today" as owners sharing this owner's effective registration date (the same key the existing daily-limit rule counts on), and evaluated the flag at create time excluding the owner being created — so the 82nd owner of a day is the first to be flagged. This matches both the spec wording ("more than 80 owners have *already* been created") and the test comment that the >80 branch "shares the same accumulation path exercised by the daily-limit rule."
